# [TASK] Share the agent contract, skills, hooks and MCP config with Antigravity

## Task
Make Antigravity work from the same contract, skills, hooks and MCP servers as Claude Code, without creating a second copy of the rules to keep in sync.

## Parent Story
Parent: #245

## Scope
Agent configuration only, no application code.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] One real contract file, with the other tools' paths symlinked to it, so all paths are byte-identical
- [x] The autonomous lock/halt path stays shared across tools, and the contract says why — two lock paths would let two agents race
- [x] The skills directory is shared rather than copied
- [x] The graphify guard hook works under Antigravity's hook contract, which differs from Claude Code's on both input and output
- [x] The hook degrades to allowing the call on bad input, an unknown tool, or a missing graphify binary
- [x] MCP servers available in Antigravity match Claude Code's

## Estimate
**Hours:** 3

## Notes


Commit `3eed52c`.

`AGENTS.md` is the only real contract; `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `.agents/skills` are symlinks (git mode 120000, verified to survive a clean clone). All three contract paths hash identically.

The `.claude/.autonomous-lock` path is deliberately shared and the contract now says why: two tools with two lock paths would not see each other's lock and would race.

The graphify hook needed a real adapter, not a copy — Antigravity sends `{"toolCall":{...}}` and expects `{"decision":...}`, while graphify speaks Claude Code's shape. Two things only running it revealed: the guard reads its payload from stdin, and it resolves `graphify-out/` relative to cwd while Antigravity starts hooks in `.agents/`. Both are handled and documented in the script.

Hook and MCP JSON stay per-tool copies because the formats differ; the contract says to change both.
